bullets.title: August NFP is make-or-break for Sep 16 FOMC: 50/50 hike odds after Waller turns dovish
bullets.body: Fed Gov. Waller's Thursday comments walked back hawkish Jackson Hole messaging, cutting September rate-hike odds from ~70% to ~54%. Street consensus for August nonfarm payrolls is +55k (GS at +40k, JPM at +50k, UBS at +65k); a print of 40k or below likely keeps Fed on hold, while a strong number re-energizes hike bets. CPI on Sep 11 is widely seen as the more decisive FOMC input.

bullets.title: Hawkish rate regime driving yields higher; AI capex borrowing a structural force
bullets.body: Multiple strategists (UBS, Goldman, Hedgeye) converge on the view that rising 10-year yields reflect monetary policy repricing back toward a pre-2008 regime — not fiscal stress. AI infrastructure borrowing (~1% of US GDP in capex) is identified as a new structural bid on long rates, with 10yr term premium estimated at 70bps and long-run Fed funds priced at ~4.10%.

bullets.title: Hedgeye/JPM both flag Quad 2 rotation: out of semis, into large-cap growth and software
bullets.body: Hedgeye upgraded September and October to Quad 2 (rising growth + inflation), which favors large-cap over small, high-beta secular growth over defensives. The High-Beta Momentum factor (long semis / short software) crashed ~77% from June highs; the GS AI Software Long vs. Semis Short basket is up ~18% last month. JPM similarly prefers Mag7 over semis near-term, noting momentum is down 21–34% from June peaks — well outside the typical 10–15% drawdown range.

bullets.title: UBS semis cycle update: SOX -22% from peak but fundamentals intact; favor Memory and Semiscap
bullets.body: UBS raised 2026–2028 semiconductor revenue forecasts to $1.63tn / $2.43tn / $2.72tn, with memory alone at $955bn in 2026 (+315% YoY). 3MMA YoY revenue growth peaked at +138% in July and is now decelerating, but non-memory inventory days fell 7.3 days QoQ with limited signs of industry-wide overbuild. SOX trades at 20x 2028E PE; top picks are Memory, Semiscap, OSATs, and select AI logic.

bullets.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra launch revitalizes AI spend narrative; but token prices down 29%
bullets.body: OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra, claiming early AGI capability, with Goldman calling it a breakthrough that revitalizes AI spending necessity. However, the Silicon Data compute token index fell 29% in August, raising unit-economics questions: oversupply risk means lower prices may not be automatically bullish if pricing falls faster than consumption grows. Meta and Google also released new frontier models this week.

bullets.title: Nvidia acquires Hugging Face for ~$13B; total AI ecosystem commitments exceed $50B
bullets.body: Nvidia confirmed the acquisition of Hugging Face (18M+ developers, leading open-source AI platform) for $12.93B — its largest deal ever, ahead of Mellanox at $6.9B — with closing targeted for 2027 pending antitrust review. Separately, Nvidia has committed ~$30B to OpenAI and up to $10B to Anthropic, with total AI-related commitments now exceeding $50B. Nvidia's equity investment portfolio has also soared tenfold to $99B as of July 2026.

bullets.title: Software sector best month in 2 years (+17% in August); valuations back to 7.5x EV/NTM
bullets.body: The Piper Sandler Software index surged +17% in August, the best month in two years, bringing YTD returns to +7.3%. Sector valuations rebounded to 7.5x EV/NTM revenue, in line with long-term averages. Market focus is shifting to stocks with active revenue acceleration or a compelling AI narrative; top picks cited include MDB, TEAM, ANET, FIG, MSFT, ORCL.

bullets.title: VIX at year-to-date lows (~14); NDX up 6 of 8 sessions; global tech rally broadening
bullets.body: VIX compressed to ~14 (new YTD lows) with NDX up in 6 of 8 recent sessions. Asia tech led overnight — Korea +165bps, Japan +125bps, HK Tech +225bps — as frontier AI launches and Snowflake's blowout guide (FY27 revenue +4% vs Street, 36% growth) drove momentum. Nasdaq futures +0.4% pre-market; S&P futures near flat ahead of NFP.

bullets.title: Hedgeye risk ranges flip META and TSLA to Bullish; GOOGL remains Bearish
bullets.body: Hedgeye's September 4 Risk Range signals show META and TSLA flipping from Bearish to Bullish trend; SNOW added as a new Bullish signal; ORCL downgraded from Bearish to Neutral and removed from active signals. MSFT, AAPL, AMZN, NFLX, NVDA all maintain Bullish ratings. SPX and COMPQ also show Bullish trends while GOOGL remains the lone Bearish mega-cap.

bullets.title: JPM turns Tactically Cautious/Neutral; recommends reducing net-longs for 2–3 weeks
bullets.body: JPM's morning briefing shifts to a tactically cautious/neutral stance, citing unclear positioning, credit spreads likely to widen post-Labor Day, and ISM Services Prices Paid above 70 for the fifth time in six months (highest 12-month average since April 2023). Recommendation: reduce net-longs, move toward dollar-neutral or market-neutral for the next 2–3 weeks. Within tech, favor Mag7 over semis; like large-cap banks and consumer discretionary if energy pulls back.

bullets.title: Financial conditions tightening: factor rotation toward Low Vol/Quality/Value
bullets.body: 22V Research notes financial conditions have tightened since mid-August (S&P -1.7% being primary driver), which historically favors Low Volatility, Quality of Earnings, and Value factors over Momentum, Growth, and Liquidity. Price Momentum's sensitivity to financial conditions has turned negative due to AI exposure. Energy, Commercial Services, and Insurance have the strongest positive FCI sensitivity; Semis, Tech Hardware, and Autos are most negatively sensitive.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley: AI capex broadening thesis intact; 2027 spend could reach $1.5T
bullets.body: MS argues 2027 AI capex could reach ~$1.5T vs. ~$1.2T Street estimates, with scaling laws and competitive pressure sustaining spend. Market rotation from semiconductors into healthcare, financials, and software is viewed as a healthy cycle extension rather than a risk-off signal. AI infrastructure deployment delays and double-ordering are flagged as potential risks within a year, but not imminent.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley sees August disinflation supporting Fed hold; Warsh preserving optionality
bullets.body: MS economists expect core CPI at 0.23% m/m and core PCE at ~0.20% m/m for August. Annual PCE revisions could lower the 12-month core PCE rate from 3.3% to ~3.1%, primarily via software PCE updates. MS characterizes Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech as preserving optionality rather than signaling an imminent hiking cycle — a view not universally shared within the FOMC.

bullets.title: Global composite PMI hit 53.5 (highest since May 2024); EM equities tactically bullish
bullets.body: JPM's international briefing notes the global composite output PMI rose to 53.5, consistent with 3.1% annual global GDP growth. JPM is tactically long US and Asia vs. Europe, and bullish on EM given improving macro, weaker USD, and AI capex tailwinds. Hedge fund positioning reset to neutral in most regions after August de-grossing.

bullets.title: Compute futures race heats up: Nodal, CME, ICE, Architect all targeting 2026 launches
bullets.body: Four exchanges are now pursuing GPU compute futures products: CME (October 5 target, under White House review), ICE, Architect, and Nodal Exchange (end-2026). Nodal is partnering with Compute Desk on cash-settled futures on Hopper and Blackwell chips, with a structural advantage from being able to bundle power and compute hedging on a single venue. CFTC is reviewing self-certifications and can delay or deny listings.

bullets.title: AI data center IT load to grow at 25% CAGR to 370 GW by 2031 — Citi bullish EQIX, DLR
bullets.body: Citi forecasts global IT load CAGR of 25% from 121 GW in 2026 to 370 GW in 2031, with annual absorption expanding from 35 GW to 60 GW. Agentic AI and broader enterprise adoption are cited as demand drivers. EQIX is Citi's top overall pick heading into the TMT conference; LRCX is seen benefiting from AI-driven etch/deposition intensity growth.

bullets.title: Robinhood stock token controversy: AMC CEO threatens legal action, contacts SEC
bullets.body: AMC CEO Adam Aron is engaging outside securities counsel and plans to contact the SEC after Robinhood launched tokenized synthetic equity for 190+ companies — including NVDA, GOOG, and AAPL — without SEC registration. AMC argues the tokens decouple stock ownership from a company's capital-raising control and demanded Robinhood voluntarily cease trading AMC tokens.

bullets.title: Waller dovish shift seen as positive for regional banks; curve steepening trade emerging
bullets.body: Fed Gov. Waller's data-dependent pivot has reduced the 2-10 yield curve's flattening pressure (currently 42bps vs. 53bps on 8/18), creating potential for a curve re-steepening that benefits asset-sensitive regional banks. KRE is down 2.6% from its August 18 peak and at oversold RSI levels. FITB is flagged as a Sector Outperform with +0.42% NII sensitivity per 100bps rate hike; WFC rated Underperform on potential reversal of capital-markets outperformance.

bullets.title: Euro area retail sales -0.6% m/m in July; Germany -3.4% on energy price reinflation
bullets.body: Euro area retail sales volumes fell 0.6% m/m in July, reversing Q2 gains, with Germany down 3.4% m/m and Spain -0.9%; France was the only bright spot at +0.9%. The retail deflator rebounded 0.6% m/m as energy prices lifted, pressuring real spending. JPM's household spending nowcast implies 3Q growth of ~1.25% annualized, but downside risks are elevated.

bullets.title: Upstream AI supply chain in pre-mass-production mode; silicon photonics bottleneck key near-term constraint
bullets.body: Goldman notes the silicon photonics/CPO space is entering a critical pre-mass-production phase where testing bottlenecks are the primary constraint. ASML has de-rated to sub-20x 2027 EV/EBITDA from ~28x in July; a re-rating catalyst would require renewed conviction in the durability of AI capex. Names with CW laser and NPO exposure are better positioned for near-term revenue capture.
